correctness.rationale: For all real degrees >2, exact log-density-ratio derivative (z-3)/[2(nu-2+z)] plus strict Jensen and normalization proves exactly two positive density roots. The positive-negative-positive density sign diagram, together with D(0)=D(infinity)=0, proves exactly one central-mass crossing. Student tail integration and normal Mills asymptotics yield R²=nu log(1/epsilon)+2(nu-1)log R+2log(1/(A_nu sqrt(2pi)))+o(1), giving the exact 2H+log(2H)+log(8/pi)+o(1) endpoint. Large-degree expansion is explicitly attributed to Ouimet; 12 numerical cases and 7 exact polynomial checks supplement the proof only.

value.rationale: Normal approximations are used for standardized Student confidence interval calibration. The theorem gives a complete sign rule across all finite-variance degrees and all symmetric thresholds, resolving when normal intervals overstate versus understate Student central mass; the unexpectedly divergent critical radius near degree two has a sharp logarithmic and loglog rate and an additive constant. It is not merely the numerical evaluation of a preexisting approximant or a restatement of Ouimet's large-degree expansion.
